title: Extract a robot-assembly spacer with a pusher
instruction: Use the long pusher to push the spacer out through the covered channel. Put the spacer flat in the green recovery nest, return the pusher flat to its starting outline, then open both grippers and move clear. Keep both parts within the table edges throughout.
context: Robot assembly and rework can require moving a temporary spacer through an access path too small for a gripper. This task isolates indirect force transmission through that path, followed by recovery of the part and tool for subsequent robot-building operations. It is a simplified mechanical analogue, not an industrial servicing claim.
setup:
Official YAM station: matte wooden table, 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m, centre (0.360,0,0.7175) m, top z=0.7475 m, with calibrated YAM bases at (0,+0.305,0.750) and (0,-0.305,0.750) m. World x points forward from the arm-base line, y left and z up. All object orientations start at identity, axes parallel to world axes; sizes below are x,y,z in metres.
channel_left_wall: PETG box, size [0.04, 0.008, 0.03], centre [0.35, 0.082, 0.7625000000000001], fixed to table.
channel_right_wall: PETG box, size [0.04, 0.008, 0.03], centre [0.35, 0.11800000000000001, 0.7625000000000001], fixed to table.
channel_left_roof: PETG box, size [0.04, 0.012, 0.008], centre [0.35, 0.092, 0.7815000000000001], fixed to table.
channel_right_roof: PETG box, size [0.04, 0.012, 0.008], centre [0.35, 0.10800000000000001, 0.7815000000000001], fixed to table.
nest_xminus_rail: PETG box, size [0.004, 0.044, 0.008], centre [0.32599999999999996, 0.26, 0.7515000000000001], fixed to table.
nest_xplus_rail: PETG box, size [0.004, 0.044, 0.008], centre [0.374, 0.26, 0.7515000000000001], fixed to table.
nest_yminus_rail: PETG box, size [0.044, 0.004, 0.008], centre [0.35, 0.23800000000000002, 0.7515000000000001], fixed to table.
nest_yplus_rail: PETG box, size [0.044, 0.004, 0.008], centre [0.35, 0.28200000000000003, 0.7515000000000001], fixed to table.
pusher_park_mark_yminus: PETG box, size [0.264, 0.001, 0.0005], centre [0.27, 0.322, 0.74775], fixed to table.
pusher_park_mark_yplus: PETG box, size [0.264, 0.001, 0.0005], centre [0.27, 0.35800000000000004, 0.74775], fixed to table.
extraction_mark_start: PETG box, size [0.001, 0.008, 0.0005], centre [0.33, 0.064, 0.74775], fixed to table.
extraction_mark_end: PETG box, size [0.001, 0.008, 0.0005], centre [0.37, 0.064, 0.74775], fixed to table.
pusher: PETG box, size [0.26, 0.016, 0.016], centre [0.27, 0.34, 0.7555000000000001], mass 0.06 kg.
spacer: aluminium box, size [0.028, 0.024, 0.024], centre [0.351, 0.1, 0.7595000000000001], mass 0.04355 kg.
The channel opening is 28 mm wide and 30 mm high, spanning x=0.330 to 0.370 m. The two roof rails leave a 4 mm viewing slit. The nest inner area is 44 x 40 mm. Printed PETG pusher mass 60 g is an effective infill assumption. Shared static/dynamic friction 1.2/1.0 is not calibrated. Initial object jitter is zero; allow 0.5 seconds settling. All dimensions and the matching start view are supplied.
scoring:
The score is evaluated from the current state and recorded event history; partial credit is not a best-so-far score.

- **0.25:** a qualifying pusher-driven exit event is recorded; the spacer has moved at least 40 mm forward through aligned pusher contact, its complete x-bound is beyond the channel exit at x = 370 mm, and its centre remains within 10 mm of the channel centreline y = 100 mm.
- **0.50:** the 0.25 outcome has occurred, and the spacer is flat and resting in the recovery nest. Its centre must be within ±8 mm in x/y and ±4 mm in z of (350, 260, 759.5) mm; rotation error is at most 10°; speed is below 15 mm/s and spin below 0.75 rad/s.
- **1.00:** the spacer remains recovered; the pusher is back within ±12 mm in x/y and ±10 mm in z of its starting centre, with rotation error at most 10°; both grippers are at least 80% open; both TCPs are at least 80 mm from the pusher and spacer bounds; the pusher speed is below 10 mm/s and spin below 0.5 rad/s. These release and stability conditions must hold continuously for one second.
- **0.00:** no qualifying outcome or a permanent failure. Either required object leaving the table is a permanent failure: every part’s complete bounds must remain inside x = −190 to 910 mm and y = −650 to 650 mm, with its underside no lower than 10 mm below the tabletop (solver tolerance). Directly transferring the spacer without the qualifying pusher event does not score. Breaking a release or stability condition clears the one-second dwell.

The evaluator estimates contact from pose, orientation, full oriented-box separation tests, transverse bounds overlap, and frame-to-frame motion. It permits up to 2.001 mm oriented-box separation and a rear-face axial gap from −4 to +2.001 mm; tool/spacer long axes must be within 10° of the channel and a long face within 5° of horizontal. Both bodies must stay near table height. Any paired positive forward displacements above a 1-nanometre numerical epsilon accumulate toward the 40 mm stroke, without an imposed push-speed range; backward motion subtracts credit before the exit event. The first full exit must occur in aligned contact after at least 25 mm of verified stroke, otherwise a permanent zero-score failure applies. The reported displacement and contact are a geometric proxy; they are not force measurements. The exact implementation and tolerances are in `src/spacer_extraction/tracker.py` and `src/spacer_extraction/evaluation_io.py`.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz); early completion only after the full-score released state holds continuously for one second.
reset_notes: Nothing consumed. Restore both arms and every object to the documented fixed layout, zero object velocities, clear event history, settle for 0.5 seconds. object_jitter=0; recorded Inspect reset seed 1415158438. Initial score 0.0.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with physical frictional grasping, pushing and collision in the official YAM Isaac Lab-Arena station. No automatic grasp attachment, teleport, insertion snap, calibrated press-fit/jam force, elasticity or damage model. Fixed PETG fixtures, effective printed pusher mass, and shared material friction are approximations. Contact and causal displacement are inferred from oriented-box geometry and paired motion at 20 Hz, with a 2.001 mm contact tolerance; they are not measured contact forces. 240 Hz physics; 14 absolute joint targets and three 320 x 176 RGB policy cameras at 20 Hz. Only joint positions and camera images reach Dream; raw evaluation state is separate.
